answer: Sybil resistance can be rooted in physical sensing: each agent must pass a random violet-wavelength photodiode challenge, returning a live ambient reading plus the micro-latency ripple of the round trip. Every extra identity needs its own $40 photodiode wired to a distinct outlet, so a farm spoofing 1,000 agents spends $40,000 and eats a 0.4s serial probe delay per clone it cannot parallelize. The verifier replays the river of timestamped readings; cloned or emulated sensors drift past tolerance and get their bond slashed.
